original_question:
Fix d in {2, 3}, let v_0 in H^1(R^d) be initial data for the cubic focusing NLS that produce a finite-time blow-up solution v at time T > 0, and let v_epsilon be the solution of the regularized equation

 i partial_t v + Delta v + (1 + f(epsilon^r |v|^2)) |v|^2 v = 0

with the same initial data. What is the limiting behavior of v_epsilon(t) as epsilon tends to 0 for times t > T, that is, after the blow-up time of the unregularized cubic NLS has already passed?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1.1, Open Problem 2: the post-blow-up ε→0 behavior of solutions to Eq. (51), the nonlinear regularization of the focusing cubic NLS in dimensions 2 and 3.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the ambient space H^1(ℝ^d), the relevant dimensions d = 2 or 3, the reference dynamics given by the focusing cubic NLS with a finite-time blow-up at T > 0, the modified equation with the same initial data, and the central post-blow-up regime t > T in which one asks what happens as ε → 0.
missing_details: The exact target is not a theorem or conjecture but Open Problem 2 in Section 4.1.1.

The modified equation is the special case of the general model (3) obtained by setting P2 = I, α2 = 0, and α3 = 0; i.e. no off-axis dependence, no damping, no self-steepening, and no ionization terms.
The paper’s scope is the no/anomalous GVD setting: d = 2 corresponds to no GVD, and d = 3 corresponds to anomalous GVD.
The unknowns are complex-valued functions v, vε : (0,∞) × ℝ^d → ℂ, Δ is the spatial Laplacian on ℝ^d, and the parameter r is assumed positive.

In the paper, f is not an arbitrary regularizer: the discussion in Section 4.1.1 concerns the standard nonlinear corrections, namely either the cubic-quintic case f(s) = -s, or a saturated nonlinearity with f(0) = 0 and s(1 + f(s)) bounded on ℝ+.
To be fully stand-alone, the unregularized equation should be written explicitly as i∂t v + Δv + |v|^2 v = 0 with v(0) = v0.
The paper does not assume that vε(t) has a single limit in a specified topology; its wording is broader: describe the behavior of vε(t) as ε → 0 for t > T.

The nearby context records known facts that frame the question: in d = 2 one has vε(t) → v(t) in H^1(ℝ^2) on [0,T) and ||vε(T)||H^1 → ∞, and partial post-blow-up scenario restrictions are known from the cited literature.

Since the question concerns times t > T, it is helpful to state that for the nonlinear modifications treated in Section 4.1.1 the modified dynamics do not undergo the same finite-time breakdown as the cubic NLS.
refined_question: Let d ∈ {2,3}, with d = 2 corresponding to the no-GVD case and d = 3 to the anomalous-GVD case, let r > 0, and let v0 ∈ H^1(ℝ^d). Assume that the solution v of the focusing cubic NLS i∂t v + Δv + |v|^2v = 0 on ℝ^d with v(0) = v0 blows up in finite time T > 0. For the corresponding solution vε of the nonlinear regularization i∂t vε + Δvε + (1 + f(ε^r|vε|^2))|vε|^2vε = 0, vε(0) = v0, where f is one of the standard nonlinear corrections considered in Section 4.1.1 of the paper—either f(s) = -s (cubic-quintic case) or a smooth saturated nonlinearity with f(0) = 0 and s(1 + f(s)) bounded on ℝ+—describe the behavior of vε(t) as ε → 0 for times t > T, i.e. after the blow-up time of the cubic NLS solution.
justification: The draft is essentially aiming at Open Problem 2, and it matches that problem almost verbatim. The only substantive paper-faithfulness issues are that the problem lives in the special Section 4.1.1 regime of Eq. (3) with P2 = I, α2 = 0, α3 = 0, and that the nonlinear correction f is not arbitrary but belongs to the standard cubic-quintic or saturated classes discussed there. The surrounding paragraph immediately before Open Problem 2 supplies the key hidden context: known convergence before blow-up in dimension 2, the divergence of the H^1 norm at the blow-up time for the regularized model, and partial classification results after blow-up. Section 4.5 later points back to Open Problem 2 as one of the reasons longer-time justification near focusing remains open.
